title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of a typescript that matches P. Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques : formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', published in Modular Functions of One Variable IV, LNM 476 (1975), §1. Grothendieck kept a copy in this dossier on Gauss–Manin connections, presumably as background for Picard–Fuchs and Cartier-operator computations on the Legendre/Weierstrass family.

Setting: p: E → S is a generalized elliptic curve, proper and flat with geometric fibres of arithmetic genus 1 (possibly singular). It has a section e (the origin, also written o) through the smooth locus. Put ω = o*Ω^1_{E/S}.

Step 1 (end of the previous page). Because p is a relative complete intersection, Rp^!O_S is concentrated in one degree. That sheaf is invertible and is called Ω^reg_{E/S}, the relative dualizing sheaf. Duality gives R^1p_*Ω^reg ≅ O_S. Hence p_*Ω^reg is locally free and commutes with base change, and fibrewise one gets p_*Ω^reg ≅ o*Ω^1 = ω.

Step 2 (this page). The adjoint of the inverse map, p*ω → Ω^reg, is an isomorphism, so the dualizing sheaf is trivialized by pullback from the base. Sections of Ω^reg coming from ω are the invariant differentials.

Step 3. Fix a nowhere-vanishing section π of ω. The filtration of p_*O(3e) by the p_*O(me), with graded pieces O, ω^{-2}, ω^{-3} (formula (1.1)), lets one choose a Zariski-local basis (y, x, 1) with:
- x ∈ p_*O(2e) mapping to π^{⊗-2} in ω^{⊗-2};
- y ∈ p_*O(3e) mapping to −π^{⊗-3} in ω^{⊗-3}.
In a local parameter t at e this means x ~ t^{-2} and y ~ −t^{-3}. The sign is chosen so that the invariant differential dx/(2y + a1x + a3) restricts to π at the origin.

Step 4. Changing π to π' = uπ changes the basis by the standard Weierstrass coordinate change (1.2): x = u²x' + r, y = u³y' + su²x' + t.

Step 5. O(3e) is very ample, so (x : y : 1) embeds E into P²_S. Comparing sections of p_*O(6e) through the graded pieces (done on the next page) shows the image satisfies a unique long Weierstrass equation (1.3), y² + a1xy + a3y = x³ + a2x² + a4x + a6.

Purpose: this is the scheme-theoretic foundation of Tate's Weierstrass formulary (b_i, c_i, Δ, j) over an arbitrary base. In this dossier it serves as the coordinate set-up for writing the Gauss–Manin connection and Picard–Fuchs equation of the universal Weierstrass family.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. The normalisations are mutually consistent: x' ↦ π'^{-2} = u^{-2}π^{-2} gives u²x' ↦ π^{-2}, and y' ↦ −π'^{-3} gives u³y' ↦ −π^{-3}.

Minor imprecision: the bijection p*ω → Ω^reg is called 'the arrow adjoint to the inverse arrow'. The relevant fact is that the trace-type map p_*Ω^reg ≅ ω is an isomorphism and its adjoint p*ω → Ω^reg is then an isomorphism, checked fibrewise. This is standard, but the 'réf' marginalia on the previous page indicate references were still to be supplied.

ideas.what: Ω^reg_{E/S} defined as the single nonzero cohomology sheaf of Rp^!O_S for a relative complete intersection curve, identified with p*ω.
ideas.modern_name: Relative dualizing sheaf of a generalized elliptic curve; triviality ω_{E/S} ≅ p*ω
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck duality (Hartshorne, Residues and Duality 1966); for elliptic curves, Deligne–Rapoport 1973 and Deligne's Formulaire 1975
ideas.where_published: Deligne, 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire d'après J. Tate', LNM 476 (1975), §1; duality theory in Hartshorne's Residues and Duality

ideas.what: Choice of Weierstrass coordinates x, y via the filtration of p_*O(3e), normalized by a trivialization π of ω, and the transformation law (1.2) under π' = uπ.
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass equations over a general base; admissible coordinate changes (u, r, s, t)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (formulary, ca. 1965-1972), written up by Deligne (1975)
ideas.where_published: Deligne, LNM 476 (1975); Katz–Mazur, Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves (1985), ch. 2

ideas.what: O(3e) is very ample, so (x, y, 1) embeds E as a plane cubic satisfying the long Weierstrass equation (1.3).

deep.surprise_reason: The page appears to be a copy of Deligne's published 'Formulaire d'après Tate' (LNM 476, 1975), §1, reproducing standard material on Weierstrass equations over a base. Its only interest is archival: it shows Grothendieck used this formulary as input for his Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs computations. It holds no new or uncredited mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Left margin, next to the line 'p_*O(2e), et que son image dans ω^{⊗-2}…': a blue handwritten annotation reading roughly 'G?' (or 'G7'), likely a reader's query or cross-reference. It is omitted in the transcription.
Bottom-left corner: handwritten '5' (archive folio number), omitted.
'o*' in the first display is the origin/zero section e (o*Ω^1_{E/S} = ω), not the letter 'o' as a variable.
In the second display the arrow is a tilde isomorphism p*ω ⥲ Ω^reg_{E/S}, followed by a period, as transcribed.
The superscript on the second π in 'soit π^{⊗-2}' is typed with an overstruck ⊗; the reading π^{⊗-2} is correct.
